newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung Elec sees sharp DRAM price rise.
newsitem.headline: Samsung Elec sees sharp DRAM price rise.

text.p: South Korea's Samsung Electronics Co expects the unit spot price for 16-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips to be $13-$14 in the second quarter, up from around $9 on average in the first quarter, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.
"We see the unit price possibly going up to as high as $15 during the period, with the average at between $13-$14," Yoon Jong-jin told Reuters.
He said reduced production by Japanese and South Korean makers since late last year was the biggest reason for this year's price recovery.
South Korean memory chip makers saw their profits plunge last year, as per-unit prices for 16-megabit DRAMs fell more than 80 percent from about $50 to $6.
Yoon declined to forecast the company's annual sales and profits for this year in the memory chip sector.
He said rising global sales of personal computers with multimedia extention (MMX) central processing units (CPUs) also boosted DRAM demand.
Personal computers with MMX CPUs, developed to strengthen function capabilities in handling multimedia data, require a higher basic memory capacity than conventional ones.
Late last year, Samsung cut its DRAM production by about 20 percent to ease a global oversupply that sparked the freefall in memory chip price, Yoon said.
